newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Philippines news bolsters Pakistani rice prices.
newsitem.headline: Philippines news bolsters Pakistani rice prices.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are expected to rise on news that the Philippines plans to buy from Asian markets, dealers said on Thursday.
An official of the state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan (RECP) said the Philippines had shown interest in buying rice but had not given any orders for the IRRI-6 variety.
"We don't have IRRI-6 and the Philippines have to buy from the private exporters," said the official, who asked not to be named.

The Philippine National Food Authority will shop for more rice from its Asian neighbours to bolster the country's buffer stocks before July this year, an official of the authority told Reuters in Manila on Thursday.
The RECP official said IRRI-6 prices were likely to rise on firm orders from the Philippines.
IRRI-6 prices had gone up to $210/215 per tonne FOB from $200/205 a week ago on foreign buying interest, he said.
Chairman Javed Islam Agha of the Lahore-based Rice Exporters Association of Pakistan said IRRI-6 prices had not yet moved although a sharp rise was expected.
He said rates of super basmati variety rice had risen sharply due to holdings by large investors who had diverted funds from other sectors into rice after making solid profits in the past two years.
"Large investors are holding super basmati on hopes that prices will rise further," said Agha, who had no estimate of holding stocks. "They will offload on further rise in prices."
Agha said exporters were not receiving significant orders from the Gulf. He attributed the low orders due to Moslem Eid al-Fitr festival which ended early this week.
"We hope the Gulf buyers will enter the Pakistani rice market in the next few weeks," Agha said.
One exporter in Karachi said Iraqis had purchased 12,500 tonnes of IRRI-6 rice from a private exporter.
Rice exports rose 83.24 percent to 217,876 tonnes worth $55 million in December from 118,899 tonnes worth $32 million in November.
In the first half of 1996/97 (July-June), rice exports rose 10.58 percent to 654,966 tonnes worth $195 million, compared to 592,300 tonnes worth $200 million in the year-ago period.
